findings.note: Candidate preserves the registry text exactly. Its 'Metso e hola butle' reads as roots grow slowly rather than explicitly 'roots slow down'; this is an existing localized sentence, so do not treat the candidate as a correction of it.
'Tshireletso e bonolo' conveys the simple protection framing. Both-side reachability and permanent paths remain exact English, preserving the access geometry.
Exact width range, reach from either path, and never-touching the growing area remain English. 'Ke yona working number' conveys that this is the working number; no geometry or numeric change.
Preserved text retains the question about reaching the middle without stepping inside and the try-before-planting instruction.
Preserved text retains that no one bed shape suits every place.
The complete least-disturbance and solves-your-problem condition stays exact English; only 'Qala ka' supplies the ordinary start framing.
'Boholo ba' retains most-scope. No-dig and build-fertility-on-top remain explicit. 'Structure' is retained as a technical term, with 'Tlohela ... e le jwalo' preserving leave it as it is.
Wet-clay prohibition and the severe compaction/poor drainage trigger, identify-the-cause step, local advice, and before-deeper-cultivation order are all preserved verbatim.
Raised beds are said to suit wet ground; the drainage-away condition remains exact English. No claim that raised beds solve drainage is added.
Sunken beds are said to suit dry ground; the desire to catch and hold the rain received remains exact English. No universal suitability claim is added.
Preserved text retains observation after heavy rain, sitting/runoff, and combining that observation with soil/drainage advice before bed choice.
The translated introduction conveys that some crops do not like root disturbance. The direct-sowing comparison and the exact crop list Beans, carrots and maize remain English.
Repaired candidate now holds the complete source paragraph in exact English, preserving the protected nursery-start/transplanting sequence and the exact tomatoes/brassicas group membership.
Spacing guidance for crop, variety and local conditions, plus packet/local-grower advice, remain exact English. The translated ending retains observing crowding as plants grow/develop.
Repaired candidate translates the timing (`Pele o lema`) and retains `mark the bed out` exactly, preserving the boundary/layout action.
Width 1.2 metres, length 3 metres, and one practice bed remain in source order. No number or unit changed.
Pegs and string remain named; the rectangle is marked and both access paths are explicitly preserved. No alternate geometry is introduced.
Repaired candidate holds the complete paragraph in exact English, preserving prepare-for-your-own-soil meaning, no-dig-first order, and digging deeper only if genuinely needed.

Both once-existing conditions and their order are retained: keep paths once present; protect the growing area once present. 'Mohala wa thapo' is recognizable as a string/rope line, and the idea-to-decision relation is preserved.
The easier-to-improve result, every-season timing, and causal explanation that people stopped stepping/walking on the bed are retained.
